title: Mobil Oil Corp. v. Federal Power Commission (1973)
shortTitle: Mobil Oil Corp. v. Federal Power Commission (1973)
summary: Before Vermont Yankee, the court derived an opportunity to test technical rate evidence from substantial-evidence review despite the absence of a formal-rulemaking requirement.

sections.Parties: Mobil Oil and other petitioners sought review of a Federal Power Commission rate order.
sections.Material Facts: The FPC set minimum pipeline transportation rates for liquid hydrocarbons. Petitioners challenged allocation of pipeline costs between gaseous and liquid products and the absence of an opportunity to cross-examine supporting evidence. The agency argued that statutory language requiring a hearing triggered only § 553 under Florida East Coast Railway.
sections.Procedural History: The D.C. Circuit agreed that formal rulemaking was not statutorily required but demanded greater opportunities to contest the factual basis. The note excerpt supplies that rationale, not the complete disposition of all objections.
sections.Issue: Could substantial-evidence review of technical ratemaking require procedural opportunities beyond ordinary written comments when formal rulemaking was not mandatory?
sections.Holding: The court required a broader opportunity to introduce adverse evidence and criticize the agency’s factual premises under the approach reported in this pre-Vermont Yankee decision.
sections.Reasoning: The court reasoned that review of the whole record required evidence both supporting and opposing the factual rate determinations, and that ordinary comments were not a reliable means to produce the needed testing. The casebook presents that reasoning as historical background to Vermont Yankee’s rejection of general judicial authority to add preferred rulemaking procedures, not as an unqualified contemporary rule.

topics.lrs-o-rulemaking-record: The pre-Vermont Yankee court inferred an opportunity to test technical evidence from the whole record needed for substantial-evidence review.
topics.lrs-n-substantial-evidence: The court derived the right to test technical evidence from the substantial-evidence standard applicable to the rate order.
topics.lrs-o-hearing-trigger: The court accepted that the statutory 'hearing' language did not trigger formal rulemaking under Florida East Coast, then built a hybrid instead.
